bonuses.requirements: EU authorities recognize Circle's USDC as 'significant' under MiCA | HTX InsightsHomeCrypto NewsIndepth ResearchEU authorities recognize Circl...EU authorities recognize Circle's USDC as 'significant' under MiCAcryptonews.ruPublished on 2026-10-14Last updated on 2026-10-14AbstractThe European Banking Authority (EBA) has classified Circle's USDC stablecoin as a "significant" electronic money token under the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation. This designation, shared by only 45 other projects, subjects USDC to joint oversight by the EBA and France's Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution. As the world's second-largest stablecoin with a $73 billion market capitalization, USDC's new status comes amid EU-based issuers seeking regulated dollar-pegged stablecoins in the region. While European regulators cannot eliminate such dollar-linked tokens, they can enforce protective measures and rules for their issuers.#USDC Price#USDC Regular Invest#USDC Surge#USDC Plunge#Classification#electronic money#EU#European Banking Authority#Market Cap#MiCA#Regulation#Stablecoin#Supervision#USDCThe European Banking Authority (EBA) has classified the $USDC stablecoin from Circle as a significant electronic money token under the European Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) legislation.In a notice published on Wednesday, the banking regulator stated that the electronic money token classification, granted to only 45 other projects, effectively means the $USDC stablecoin will be under the joint supervision of the EBA and the French supervisory authority — the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution. The stablecoin ranks second in market capitalization: $73 billion versus $184 billion for Tether USDt.The 'significant' status comes at a time when many EU-based token issuers have been striving for regulated, dollar-pegged stablecoins in the region. A significant transfer of 24,544 $ETH, valued at approximately $60 million, was recorded moving from an unknown wallet to the Beacon Depositor. This activity, reported by the crypto commentator @whale_alert, raises questions about potential shifts in market sentiment and trading behavior. As Ethereum continues to evolve, monitoring such movements can provide insights into broader market trends.

Inside the Move
The recent transfer of 24,544 $ETH to the Beacon Depositor underscores a notable shift in Ethereum’s market dynamics. Such movements often indicate shifts in investor sentiment, particularly among larger holders or ‘whales.’ With the broader crypto market displaying mixed signals, this transfer could reflect both opportunistic positioning and changing trader expectations. The lack of accompanying trading volume suggests that this transfer may not be driven by immediate trading pressures, but rather strategic positioning within Ethereum’s staking ecosystem.

Market Pulse
Ethereum’s recent activity highlights its ongoing significance within the crypto landscape, particularly with the Beacon Depositor’s role in staking. As the network evolves, substantial transfers like this often precede broader market movements, potentially influencing overall sentiment among traders. The absence of immediate price changes indicates that this transfer is part of a longer-term strategic play rather than day-to-day trading maneuvers.

Ethereum is a leading blockchain platform known for its smart contract functionality and extensive ecosystem. The Beacon Depositor plays a crucial role in Ethereum 2.0, facilitating staking and enhancing network security. He argues that their role in facilitating illicit transactions justifies a potential ban. Key Details

Li Lu claims cryptocurrency will ultimately disappear due to its flaws. He argues that a currency’s effectiveness requires enforcement mechanisms. Lu advocates for a ban on crypto, citing its role in illicit transactions. He warns that short-term performance focus can lead to speculation. His remarks were made during an interview at Columbia Business School.
The Numbers

Currently, the broader crypto market shows mixed signals, with key assets fluctuating amid varied investor sentiment. Bitcoin miners plunge up to 13% in Wall Street’s worst selloff since July | HTX InsightsHomeCrypto NewsBitcoin miners plunge up to 13...Bitcoin miners plunge up to 13% in Wall Street’s worst selloff since JulycointelegraphPublished on 2026-10-15Last updated on 2026-10-15AbstractU.S. stocks experienced their sharpest selloff since July, driven by hotter-than-expected inflation data. The S&P 500 fell 1.1%, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.9%. Technology and AI infrastructure stocks were notably hit, with Bitcoin miners plunging as much as 13%. Companies like CoreWeave, Nebius, and Oracle saw significant declines.

The selloff extended to Bitcoin mining firms, many of which have expanded into AI infrastructure. TeraWulf, Core Scientific, Cipher Mining, and IREN all dropped over 12%. The downturn is partly attributed to concerns that higher interest rates could increase borrowing costs for data center expansion.

September's U.S. consumer prices rose 3.7% year-over-year, exceeding forecasts and the Fed's 2% target, largely due to higher gasoline prices. This data briefly boosted expectations for an October Fed rate hike, though San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly indicated there was no urgency to act immediately.#AI#Bitcoin#CPI#Fed#Inflation#Infrastructure#Miners#Selloff#Stocks#TechnologyUS stocks suffered their sharpest selloff since July on Wednesday as hotter-than-expected inflation data weighed on technology and AI infrastructure companies, with Bitcoin miners among those hit. The S&P 500 fell 1.1%, its biggest one-day decline since July 29; the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.9%, its biggest one-day drop since July 23, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.1% over the day. Leading decliners among major tech companies included data center operator CoreWeave, which fell 16%, AI infrastructure provider Nebius, which fell 11%, and Oracle, which fell 9%.
